categories.main_business_segments: Cosmo Chemical Co., Ltd. operates primarily in four business segments: Cobalt sulfate production for secondary battery cathode materials, titanium dioxide manufacturing and sales, advanced materials including battery cathode active materials and functional films, and catalysts production. The company also engages in waste battery recycling and related new energy businesses such as electric vehicles and renewable energy storage systems.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes chemical extraction processes to produce cobalt sulfate from cobalt ore and scrap materials. Titanium dioxide is manufactured through chemical reaction of titanium ilmenite ore with sulfuric acid, producing anatase-type TiO2. Advanced materials include manufacturing of cathode active materials for lithium-ion batteries and functional films using coating technologies. The catalyst segment produces zeolites and selective catalytic reduction (SCR) catalysts using inorganic chemical synthesis and system integration methods. The company is also developing proprietary recycling technologies for lithium-ion battery scrap recovery.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include battery manufacturers, electric vehicle producers, semiconductor and electronics companies, and chemical product manufacturers. The cobalt sulfate and cathode materials serve the secondary battery industry, while titanium dioxide products are supplied to plastics, paints, rubber, paper, and textile industries. The catalyst products target automotive emission control and environmental treatment sectors. The company also serves global markets with exports to Japan, Southeast Asia, Europe, and the Americas.
categories.geographic_coverage: Cosmo Chemical operates mainly in South Korea with manufacturing facilities in Ulsan, Onsan, and Chungju. It imports raw materials from India, Australia, Vietnam, and China. The company exports titanium dioxide and advanced materials to over 40 countries including Japan, Southeast Asia, Europe, and the Americas. It also has subsidiaries in Korea and investments in China.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates primarily upstream and midstream in the supply chain, producing raw and intermediate materials such as cobalt sulfate, titanium dioxide, cathode active materials, and catalysts. It sources raw ores and chemicals, processes them into specialized chemical products, and supplies these to battery manufacturers, chemical producers, and industrial customers. It is expanding downstream into recycling of spent lithium-ion batteries to recover valuable metals.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding the secondary battery materials business, especially recycling of lithium-ion battery scrap to extract nickel, cobalt, and lithium. The company invests in high value-added titanium dioxide products such as ultrafine and purified grades. R&D focuses on developing cobalt-free and high-nickel cathode materials, advanced functional films for electronics, and environmental catalysts. The company aims to enhance production technologies, develop new products, and increase market share in emerging energy and environmental sectors.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through product sales of cobalt sulfate, titanium dioxide, cathode active materials, functional films, and catalysts. The company also earns income from waste battery recycling operations and related processed materials. Additional revenue streams include licensing, technical services, and rental income from real estate. Sales are conducted via direct contracts with industrial customers and exports.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In titanium dioxide, competitors include global majors such as Kronos, Lomon, Venator, Tronox, and Chemours. Cosmo Chemical holds a dominant domestic position as the sole Korean producer of anatase-type TiO2 with about 70% domestic market share. In battery materials, it competes with international chemical and battery material suppliers. The catalyst segment faces competition from specialized chemical companies. The company leverages proprietary technology, quality, and integrated supply chain to maintain competitiveness.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of 2023, Cosmo Chemical reported consolidated revenues of approximately 799 billion KRW, an 11.2% increase year-over-year, with operating profit declining by 92.7% to 3 billion KRW due to raw material price fluctuations. Total assets grew 35.1% to about 1.09 trillion KRW, supported by investments in battery materials and recycling facilities. The company has increased capital through multiple rights offerings to fund expansion. The advanced materials segment showed strong revenue growth, while cobalt sulfate and titanium dioxide segments faced price pressure.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Cosmo Chemical emphasizes its unique position as the only Korean producer extracting cobalt sulfate directly from ore, ensuring consistent high-quality battery materials. It offers a diversified titanium dioxide product portfolio including high-purity and ultrafine grades tailored for specialized applications. The company’s integrated recycling technology for lithium-ion batteries provides cost-effective raw material sourcing and sustainability benefits. Its long-standing customer relationships, proprietary technologies, and focus on high value-added products differentiate it in competitive global markets.
